context.narrative_job: Tell a cold viewer that sale readiness is a one-person business they can build, prove the idea is concrete with one usable dependency-mapping exercise, and route the service design to the full episode.
context.viewer_before: The conversation-first cut invited the viewer into the opportunity but described the practice as something Manav was exploring, which made the BUILD position sound uncertain.
context.viewer_after: The viewer hears a direct answer, understands that a sale-readiness practice is a business they can build before a buyer appears, learns one useful diagnostic, and retains willingness to pay as the specific unknown.

data.choice: Open with HOW DO YOU GET A BUSINESS READY TO SELL?, answer that the work starts before a buyer exists, and state YOU CAN BUILD A BUSINESS AROUND THAT PREPARATION: A SALE-READINESS PRACTICE. Preserve 30 DAYS. NO OWNER. as the first test and the complete dependency-map payoff. Close by asking whether an owner would pay before a buyer appears, then promise that the full episode shows how to build the service. The revised scratch cut runs 43.846410 seconds.
data.reason: Authority belongs on the recommendation the episode has earned: this is a service model worth building. Uncertainty belongs on market proof, not on Manav's command of the model. The split gives the viewer a confident way in without fabricating demand.

alternatives.choice: Keep saying that Manav is exploring the opportunity.
alternatives.reason_not_selected: The owner explicitly rejected that posture because it weakens the BUILD recommendation and makes the presenter sound unsure of the business being taught.

alternatives.choice: Call sale readiness a big or proven opportunity.
alternatives.reason_not_selected: No current evidence establishes market size or willingness to pay before a buyer appears. Authority does not require inventing validation.

alternatives.choice: Promise to help someone sell their business.
alternatives.reason_not_selected: That wording can imply the preparation causes a sale. Get their business ready to sell accurately names the service boundary.

reuse.applies_when: An OE companion Short is built from an episode with a supported BUILD recommendation but unresolved customer demand.
reuse.avoid_when: The episode itself has not earned a build recommendation or the Short would have to imply proven demand, a customer outcome or market size.

animation.form: Avatar-led direct address, followed by an authoritative business card, an earned question/title reveal and a working dependency map.
animation.entry: Manav and HOW DO YOU GET A BUSINESS READY TO SELL? establish the conversation immediately.
animation.change: The question clears, A BUSINESS YOU CAN BUILD names the sale-readiness practice, and that card clears before 30 DAYS. NO OWNER. becomes the first test.
animation.hold: The map settles long enough to deliver a complete first working diagnostic before the commercial question.
animation.exit: Manav returns with the willingness-to-pay question; THE FULL EPISODE SHOWS YOU HOW TO BUILD THE SERVICE gives the continuation authority while the Related Video target stays explicitly pending.

nuance.performance: This remains a static V5 identity hold with local system scratch voice. It tests thought sequence, avatar prominence and phone comprehension; final warmth, lift, gesture, articulation and lip sync remain untested.
nuance.false_inference: The Short recommends the sale-readiness practice as a business model. It does not claim proven demand, a large market, a validated diagnostic, a successful sale, preserved valuation or a successful service outcome.
nuance.source_basis: Exact owner feedback, Content OS first-listen and authority controls, the EP007 BUILD recommendation, OE Shorts discovery precedent, and the current Short 01 prototype.
